   // Try to get log_dir from the heartbeat record's workspace.\n        // Default to ~/.needle/logs if not configured.\n        let log_dir =\n            std::env::var_os(\"HOME\").map(|h| PathBuf::from(h).join(\".needle\").join(\"logs\"))?;\n\n        Some(log_dir.join(format!(\"{}-{}.jsonl\", worker_id, session_id)))\n    }\n\n    /// Read the last N events from a JSONL file.\n    ///\n    /// Returns lines in reverse order (newest first), limited to scan_events.\n    fn read_jsonl_tail(&self, path: &Path, scan_events: usize) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read jsonl: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        let lines: Vec<&str> = content.lines().collect();\n        let tail_len = scan_events.min(lines.len());\n        let mut tail = Vec::with_capacity(tail_len);\n\n        for line in lines.iter().rev().take(tail_len) {\n            tail.push(line.to_string());\n        }\n\n        Ok(tail)\n    }\n\n    /// Scan live workers for loop patterns.\n    ///\n    /// Returns workers with fresh heartbeats that exhibit stuck-loop behavior.\n    fn scan_live_loops(&self) -> Result<Vec<LiveLoopWorker>> {\n        let mut looping = Vec::new();\n\n        if !self.config.detect_live_loops {\n            return Ok(looping);\n        }\n\n        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&self.heartbeat_dir) {\n            Ok(e) => e,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n                tracing::debug!(\"splice: heartbeat directory does not exist\");\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                return Err(e).context(\"failed to read heartbeat directory\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        for entry in entries {\n            let entry = match entry {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            let path = entry.path();\n            if path.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) != Some(\"json\") {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Parse the heartbeat file.\n            let content = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {\n                Ok(c) => c,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            let record: HeartbeatRecord = match serde_json::from_str(&content) {\n                Ok(r) => r,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Skip stale heartbeats — those are handled by scan_failed_workers.\n            let elapsed = Utc::now() - record.last_heartbeat;\n            let stale_threshold_secs = self.config.stale_threshold_secs as i64;\n            if elapsed.num_seconds() >= stale_threshold_secs {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Check for loop patterns in the JSONL tail.\n            let log_path = match self.worker_log_path(&record.worker_id, &record.session) {\n                Some(p) => p,\n                None => continue,\n            };\n\n            if !log_path.exists() {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            if let Some(loop_worker) = self.check_worker_for_loops(&record, &log_path)? {\n                looping.push(loop_worker);\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(looping)\n    }\n\n    /// Check a single worker's JSONL for loop patterns.\n    ///\n    /// Returns Some(LiveLoopWorker) if a pattern is detected, None otherwise.\n    fn check_worker_for_loops(\n        &self,\n        record: &HeartbeatRecord,\n        log_path: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<Option<LiveLoopWorker>> {\n        let tail_events = self.read_jsonl_tail(log_path, self.config.live_loop_scan_events)?;\n\n        // Parse events into structured form for analysis.\n        let mut events: Vec<TelemetryEventLike> = Vec::new();\n        for line in &tail_events {\n            if let Ok(ev) = serde_json::from_str::<TelemetryEventLike>(line) {\n                events.push(ev);\n            }\n        }\n\n        let detected_at = Utc::now();\n\n        // Pattern 1: Claim churn — repeated race_lost for same bead.\n        if let Some(churn) = self.detect_claim_churn(&events) {\n            return Ok(Some(LiveLoopWorker {\n                heartbeat: record.clone(),\n                loop_type: LoopType::ClaimChurn {\n                    bead_id: churn.bead_id,\n                    count: churn.count,\n                },\n                evidence: LoopEvidence {\n                    events_scanned: tail_events.len(),\n                    sample_events: churn.sample,\n                    detected_at,\n                },\n            }));\n        }\n\n        // Pattern 2: State ping-pong — short cycle without forward progress.\n        if let Some(pingpong) = self.detect_state_ping_pong(&events) {\n            return Ok(Some(LiveLoopWorker {\n                heartbeat: record.clone(),\n                loop_type: LoopType::StatePingPong {\n                    states: pingpong.states,\n                    cycle_count: pingpong.cycle_count,\n                },\n                evidence: LoopEvidence {\n                    events_scanned: tail_events.len(),\n                    sample_events: pingpong.sample,\n                    detected_at,\n                },\n            }));\n        }\n\n        // Pattern 3: Log runaway — excessive growth without completion.\n        // This requires checking file metadata, not just event content.\n        if let Some(runaway) = self.detect_log_runaway(record, log_path, &events)? {\n            return Ok(Some(LiveLoopWorker {\n                heartbeat: record.clone(),\n                loop_type: LoopType::LogRunaway {\n                    bytes_growth: runaway.bytes_growth,\n                    window_secs: runaway.window_secs,\n                },\n                evidence: LoopEvidence {\n                    events_scanned: tail_events.len(),\n                    sample_events: runaway.sample,\n                    detected_at,\n                },\n            }));\n        }\n\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n\n    /// Detect claim churn: repeated race_lost events for the same bead.\n    fn detect_claim_churn(&self, events: &[TelemetryEventLike]) -> Option<ClaimChurnInfo> {\n        let mut race_lost_counts: HashMap<String, u32> = HashMap::new();\n        let mut sample: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n\n        for ev in events.iter().rev() {\n            if ev.event_type == \"bead.claim.race_lost\" {\n                if let Some(bead_id) = &ev.bead_id {\n                    *race_lost_counts.entry(bead_id.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;\n                    if sample.len() < 10 {\n                        sample.push(format!(\"{} race_lost {}\", ev.timestamp, bead_id));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        for (bead_id, count) in &race_lost_counts {\n            if *count >= self.config.claim_churn_threshold {\n                return Some(ClaimChurnInfo {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    count: *count,\n                    sample,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        None\n    }\n\n    /// Detect state ping-pong: short state cycles without forward progress.\n    fn detect_state_ping_pong(&self, events: &[TelemetryEventLike]) -> Option<StatePingPongInfo> {\n        // Look for state_transition events and extract state sequences.\n        let mut state_transitions: Vec<(DateTime<Utc>, String, String)> = Vec::new();\n\n        for ev in events.iter().rev() {\n            if ev.event_type == \"worker.state_transition\" {\n                if let (Some(from), Some(to)) = (&ev.data.get(\"from\"), &ev.data.get(\"to\")) {\n                    if let (Some(from_str), Some(to_str)) = (from.as_str(), to.as_str()) {\n                        state_transitions.push((\n                            ev.timestamp,\n                            from_str.to_string(),\n                            to_str.to_string(),\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if state_transitions.len() < 8 {\n            return None; // Not enough transitions to detect a cycle.\n        }\n\n        // Check for cycles of length <= 4 states.\n        let window_size = 8.min(state_transitions.len());\n        let window: Vec<_> = state_transitions\n            .iter()\n            .take(window_size)\n            .map(|(_, _, to)| to.clone())\n            .collect();\n\n        // Count unique states in the window.\n        let unique_states: HashSet<_> = window.iter().collect();\n\n        if unique_states.len() <= 4 && window.len() >= 6 {\n            // Check if we're cycling without forward-progress events.\n            let has_forward_progress = events\n                .iter()\n                .any(|ev| matches!(ev.event_type.as_str(), \"agent.completed\" | \"bead.completed\"));\n\n            if !has_forward_progress {\n                let sample = state_transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .take(10)\n                    .map(|(ts, from, to)| format!(\"{} {} -> {}\", ts.format(\"%H:%M:%S\"), from, to))\n                    .collect();\n\n                return Some(StatePingPongInfo {\n                    states: unique_states.iter().map(|s| (*s).clone()).collect(),\n                    cycle_count: (window.len() / unique_states.len()) as u32,\n                    sample,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        None\n    }\n\n    /// Detect log runaway: excessive file growth without completion events.\n    fn detect_log_runaway(\n        &self,\n        _record: &HeartbeatRecord,\n        log_path: &Path,\n        events: &[TelemetryEventLike],\n    ) -> Result<Option<LogRunawayInfo>> {\n        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(log_path)?;\n        let file_size = metadata.len();\n\n        // Check for agent.completed events in the scanned window.\n        let has_completed = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|ev| ev.event_type == \"agent.completed\" || ev.event_type == \"bead.completed\");\n\n        if !has_completed && file_size > self.config.log_runaway_bytes {\n            // Calculate time window from oldest to newest event.\n            if let (Some(oldest), Some(newest)) = (events.first(), events.last()) {\n                let window_secs = (newest.timestamp - oldest.timestamp).num_seconds().max(1) as u64;\n\n                if window_secs <= self.config.live_loop_window_secs {\n                    let sample = events\n                        .iter()\n                        .rev()\n                        .take(10)\n                        .map(|ev| format!(\"{} {}\", ev.timestamp, ev.event_type))\n                        .collect();\n\n                    return Ok(Some(LogRunawayInfo {\n                        bytes_growth: file_size,\n                        window_secs,\n                        sample,\n                    }));\n                }\n            }\n\n            // If we can't calculate window but file is huge and no completion, still flag.\n            if file_size > self.config.log_runaway_bytes * 2 {\n                let sample = events\n                    .iter()\n                    .rev()\n                    .take(10)\n                    .map(|ev| format!(\"{} {}\", ev.timestamp, ev.event_type))\n                    .collect();\n\n                return Ok(Some(LogRunawayInfo {\n                    bytes_growth: file_size,\n                    window_secs: self.config.live_loop_window_secs,\n                    sample,\n                }));\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n\n    /// Scan for failed workers (stale heartbeat + dead tmux session).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of heartbeat records for workers that are considered dead.\n    fn scan_failed_workers(&self) -> Result<Vec<HeartbeatRecord>> {\n        let mut failed = Vec::new();\n\n        // Read all *.json files from heartbeat directory.\n        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&self.heartbeat_dir) {\n            Ok(e) => e,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n                tracing::debug!(\"splice: heartbeat directory does not exist\");\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                return Err(e).context(\"failed to read heartbeat directory\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        for entry in entries {\n            let entry = match entry {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            let path = entry.path();\n            if path.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) != Some(\"json\") {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Parse the heartbeat file.\n            let content = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {\n                Ok(c) => c,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        path = %path.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"splice: failed to read heartbeat file\"\n                    );\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            let record: HeartbeatRecord = match serde_json::from_str(&content) {\n                Ok(r) => r,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        path = %path.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"splice: failed to parse heartbeat file\"\n                    );\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            // Check if heartbeat is stale.\n            let elapsed = Utc::now() - record.last_heartbeat;\n            let stale_threshold_secs = self.config.stale_threshold_secs as i64;\n            if elapsed.num_seconds() < stale_threshold_secs {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Check if tmux session is still alive.\n            let alive = std::process::Command::new(\"tmux\")\n                .args([\"has-session\", \"-t\", &record.session])\n                .status()\n                .map(|s| s.success())\n                .unwrap_or(false);\n\n            if !alive {\n                // Session is dead — this is a failed worker.\n                failed.push(record);\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(failed)\n    }\n\n    /// Document a worker failure by creating a bead in the report workspace.\n    ///\n    /// If `report_workspace` is None or the workspace is invalid, returns Ok(())\n    /// without creating a bead.\n    async fn document_failure(&self, record: &HeartbeatRecord) -> Result<()> {\n        let report_workspace = match &self.config.report_workspace {\n            Some(ws) => ws,\n            None => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    worker_id = %record.worker_id,\n                    session = %record.session,\n                    \"splice: no report workspace configured, skipping bead creation\"\n                );\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Verify the workspace exists and has a .beads/ subdirectory.\n        let beads_dir = report_workspace.join(\".beads\");\n        if !report_workspace.exists() || !beads_dir.exists() {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                workspace = %report_workspace.display(),\n                worker_id = %record.worker_id,\n                \"splice: report workspace does not exist or has no .beads/ directory\"\n            );\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Instantiate bead store for the report workspace.\n        let store = BrCliBeadStore::discover(report_workspace.clone())\n            .context(\"failed to instantiate bead store for report workspace\")?;\n\n        // Build bead title.\n        let title = format!(\"Worker failure: {} ({})\", record.worker_id, record.session);\n\n        // Calculate elapsed time since last heartbeat.\n        let elapsed = Utc::now() - record.last_heartbeat;\n        let elapsed_secs = elapsed.num_seconds();\n        let elapsed_mins = elapsed_secs / 60;\n        let elapsed_hours = elapsed_mins / 60;\n        let elapsed_str = if elapsed_hours > 0 {\n            format!(\"{}h {}m\", elapsed_hours, elapsed_mins % 60)\n        } else if elapsed_mins > 0 {\n            format!(\"{}m\", elapsed_mins)\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{}s\", elapsed_secs)\n        };\n\n        // Build bead body.\n        let current_bead_str = record.current_bead.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"(none)\");\n        let body = format!(\n            \"## Worker Failure\\n\\n\\\n             **Worker:** {}\\n\\\n             **Session:** {}\\n\\\n             **Workspace:** {}\\n\\\n             **Last heartbeat:** {} ({} ago)\\n\\\n             **State at failure:** {}\\n\\\n             **Beads processed:** {}\\n\\\n             **Current bead:** {}\\n\\\n             **PID:** {}\\n\",\n            record.worker_id,\n            record.session,\n            record.workspace,\n            record.last_heartbeat.format(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC\"),\n            elapsed_str,\n            record.state,\n            record.beads_processed,\n            current_bead_str,\n            record.pid\n        );\n\n        // Create the bead.\n        let bead_id = store\n            .create_bead(&title, &body, &[\"worker-failure\", \"human\"])\n bead_id = %bead_id,\n            \"splice: documented worker failure\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Document a live-loop worker by creating a bead in the report workspace.\n    ///\n    /// If `report_workspace` is None or the workspace is invalid, returns Ok(())\n    /// without creating a bead.\n    async fn document_live_loop(&self, worker: &LiveLoopWorker) -> Result<()> {\n        let report_workspace = match &self.config.report_workspace {\n            Some(ws) => ws,\n            None => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    worker_id = %worker.heartbeat.worker_id,\n                    session = %worker.heartbeat.session,\n                    \"splice: no report workspace configured, skipping loop bead creation\"\n                );\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Verify the workspace exists and has a .beads/ subdirectory.\n        let beads_dir = report_workspace.join(\".beads\");\n        if !report_workspace.exists() || !beads_dir.exists() {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                workspace = %report_workspace.display(),\n                worker_id = %worker.heartbeat.worker_id,\n                \"splice: report workspace does not exist or has no .beads/ directory\"\n            );\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Instantiate bead store for the report workspace.\n        let store = BrCliBeadStore::discover(report_workspace.clone())\n            .context(\"failed to instantiate bead store for report workspace\")?;\n\n        // Build bead title and body based on loop type.\n        let (title, pattern_name, details) = match &worker.loop_type {\n            LoopType::ClaimChurn { bead_id, count } => {\n                let title = format!(\n                    \"Live loop: {} claim churn on bead {}\",\n                    worker.heartbeat.worker_id, bead_id\n                );\n                let details = format!(\n                    \"**Pattern:** Claim churn\\n\\\n                     **Bead ID:** {}\\n\\\n                     **Race-lost events (in last {}):** {}\\n\",\n                    bead_id, worker.evidence.events_scanned, count\n                );\n                (title, \"claim_churn\".to_string(), details)\n            }\n            LoopType::StatePingPong {\n bytes_growth / 1024 / 1024,\n                    window_secs\n                );\n                (title, \"log_runaway\".to_string(), details)\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Build sample events section.\n        let sample_section = if worker.evidence.sample_events.is_empty() {\n            String::new()\n        } else {\n            let samples: String = worker\n                .evidence\n                .sample_events\n                .iter()\n                .take(20)\n                .map(|s| format!(\"  - {}\\n\", s))\n                .collect();\n            format!(\n                \"\\n## Sample Events (last {} scanned)\\n\\n```\\n{}\\n```\\n\",\n                worker.evidence.events_scanned, samples\n            )\n        };\n\n        let body = format!(\n            \"## Live Worker Loop Detected\\n\\n\\\n             **Worker:** {}\\n\\\n             **Session:** {}\\n\\\n             **Workspace:** {}\\n\\\n             **Last heartbeat:** {}\\n\\\n             **State:** {}\\n\\\n             **Beads processed:** {}\\n\\\n             **Detected at:** {}\\n\\n\\\n             ## Pattern Details\\n\\n\\\n             {}{}\\n\\\n             ## %worker.heartbeat.session,\n            pattern = %pattern_name,\n            bead_id = %bead_id,\n            \"splice: documented live loop\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl super::Strand for SpliceStrand {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"splice\"\n    }\n\n    async fn evaluate(&self, _store: &dyn BeadStore) -> StrandResult {\n        if !self.config.enabled {\n            return StrandResult::NoWork;\n        }\n\n        let mut state = SpliceState::load(&self.state_dir)\n            .ok()\n            .flatten()\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n        let mut documented = 0usize;\n\n        // Scan for failed workers (stale heartbeat + dead tmux session).\n        let failed = match self.scan_failed_workers() {\n            Ok(f) => f,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"splice: failed to scan heartbeats\");\n                return StrandResult::NoWork;\n            }\n        };\n\n        for record in &failed {\n            if state.documented_sessions.contains(&record.session) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            match self.document_failure(record).await {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    state.documented_sessions.insert(record.session.clone());\n                    documented += 1;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        worker_id = %record.worker_id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"splice: failed to document worker failure\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Scan for live-but-looping workers.\n        let looping = match self.scan_live_loops() {\n            Ok(l) => l,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"splice: failed to scan for live loops\");\n                Vec::new()\n            }\n        };\n\n        for worker in &looping {\n            // Build de-duplication key: (worker_id, session_id, pattern_name)\n            let pattern_name = match &worker.loop_type {\n                LoopType::ClaimChurn { .. } => \"claim_churn\",\n                LoopType::StatePingPong { .. } => \"state_ping_pong\",\n                LoopType::LogRunaway { .. } => \"log_runaway\",\n            };\n            let key = format!(\n                \"{}-{}-{}\",\n                worker.heartbeat.worker_id, worker.heartbeat.session, pattern_name\n            );\n\n            if state.documented_loops.contains(&key) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            match self.document_live_loop(worker).await {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    state.documented_loops.insert(key);\n                    documented += 1;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        worker_id = %worker.heartbeat.worker_id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"splice: failed to document live loop\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if documented > 0 {\n            let _ = state.save(&self.state_dir);\n            tracing::info!(documented, \"splice: documented worker failures and loops\");\n            StrandResult::WorkCreated\n        } else {\n            StrandResult::NoWork\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n8\t\n9\t1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n10\t\n11\t2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n12\t\n13\t3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n14\t\n15\t4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n16\t\n17\t5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n18\t\n19\t6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## Architecture Overview\n24\t\n25\tNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n26\t\n27\t```\n28\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n29\t│                        CLI Layer                              │\n30\t│  needle run | stop | list | attach | status | config          │\n31\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n32\t│                     Worker Layer                              │\n33\t│  Worker loop, strand waterfall, session management            │\n34\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n35\t│                  Coordination Layer                            │\n36\t│  Claiming, locking, heartbeats, peer awareness                │\n37\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n38\t│                    Agent Layer                                 │\n39\t│  Adapter interface, dispatch, result capture                  │\n40\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n41\t│                   Foundation Layer                             │\n42\t│  Telemetry, configuration, bead store interface, self-healing │\n43\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n44\t```\n45\t\n46\t### Component Map\n47\t\n48\t| Component | Responsibility | Inputs | Outputs |\n49\t|-----------|---------------|--------|---------|\n50\t| **CLI** | Parse commands, manage sessions | User commands | Worker processes |\n51\t| **Worker** | Execute the strand waterfall loop | Bead queue state | Dispatch requests, state transitions |\n52\t| **StrandRunner** | Evaluate strands in sequence | Queue state, **OutcomeHandler** | Route exit code to explicit handler | Exit code, stdout/stderr | State transition |\n57\t| **Telemetry** | Structured event emission | Any component event | JSONL records |\n58\t| **HealthMonitor** | Heartbeat, stuck detection, peer awareness | Worker state | Recovery actions |\n59\t| **ConfigLoader** | Hierarchical config resolution | Files, env, CLI args | Resolved config |\n60\t| **BeadStore** | Abstract interface to bead backend | CRUD operations | Bead records |\n61\t| **Mitosis** | Split multi-task beads into children with dedup | Failed bead, parent's existing children | Child beads or no-op |\n62\t\n63\t---\n64\t\n65\t## Language Decision\n66\t\n67\tThe implementation language must provide:\n68\t\n69\t| Requirement | Why | Source |\n70\t|-------------|-----|--------|\n71\t| Exhaustive pattern matching | Every outcome must be handled; compiler enforces it | Principle 2, bead-lifecycle-bugs.md |\n72\t| Real module system | 45K single-file bash was unmaintainable | bash-at-scale-problems.md |\n73\t| Structured error types | Silent failures caused cascading bugs | claim-race-conditions.md |\n74\t| Native JSON support | Fragile jq parsing corrupted state | worker-starvation-lessons.md |\n75\t| Proper concurrency primitives | flock/trap/PID files were inadequate | concurrency-approaches-compared.md |\n76\t| Single binary distribution | NEEDLE must be trivially installable | Principle 3 |\n77\t| Cross-platform | Linux, macOS at minimum | Principle 3 |\n78\t| Static analysis | Catch undefined functions, unused variables at compile time | bundler-build-integrity.md |\n79\t\n80\t**Recommended: Rust.** Exhaustive `match`, `Result<T, E>` error handling, `serde_json`, `tokio` for async, single binary via static linking, cross-compilation. The beads ecosystem already has Rust precedent (beads_rust, beads-polis).\n81\t\n82\t**Acceptable alternative: Go.** Simpler learning curve, good concurrency, single binary. Lacks exhaustive matching (requires discipline instead of compiler enforcement).\n83\t\n84\t**Not acceptable: Bash, Python, Node.** Bash failed at scale (documented). Python/Node require runtime dependencies, violating single-binary distribution.\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## Key Decisions from Research\n89\t\n90\tThese decisions are informed by the 14 research files in `docs/research/`:\n91\t\n92\t| Decision | Chosen Approach | Alternative Considered | Why |\n93\t|----------|----------------|----------------------|-----|\n94\t| Bead store interface | Abstract trait over `br` CLI | Direct SQLite access | Platform agnostic; works with future bead backends |\n95\t| Claim atomicity | `br update --claim` + workspace flock | Central coordinator (Perles) | No SPOF; works with decentralized workers |\n96\t| Heartbeat model | File-based heartbeat with TTL (from beads-polis) | Shared memory | Survives worker crashes; observable by peers |\n97\t| Validation gates | Pluggable gate system (inspired by bg-gate) | Hardcoded checks | Different workspaces need different validation |\n98\t| Work decomposition | Built-in mitosis with child-aware dedup | External only (spec2beads) | Mitosis is valid when the split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection) and dedup checks the parent's existing children |\n99\t| Self-modification | Allowed with release channel promotion (testing → stable → fleet hot-reload) | Prohibited entirely | v1 failures came from untested changes deploying directly to the fleet. Canary testing with defined inputs/outputs prevents this. |\n100\t| Workspace discovery | Explicit configuration | Filesystem scanning | Explore strand's unbounded find caused 35+ load |\n101\t| Alert system | Verify-then-alert with rate limiting | Alert-on-empty | 100% false positive rate from naive alerting |\n102\t\n103\t## Key Decisions from Operational Learnings\n104\t\n105\tThese decisions are informed by the 9 notes files in `docs/notes/`:\n106\t\n107\t| Learning | Design Response |\n108\t|----------|----------------|\n109\t| Mitosis explosion (5,741 duplicate beads) | Mitosis checks parent's existing children before creating new ones. Duplicate splits are structurally impossible. Split criteria are semantic (multi-task detection), not numeric. |\n110\t| 100% false positive starvation alerts | Three-state model: no beads exist / all claimed / invisible. Verify independently before alerting. |\n111\t| Bundler shipped undefined functions | Compiled language eliminates this class entirely. |\n112\t| Agent-owned closure most reliable | NEEDLE does not close beads. Agent receives `br close <id>` instruction in prompt. |\n113\t| stdout/stderr corruption | Telemetry is a structured system, never interleaved with agent output. |\n114\t| Workers modifying their own orchestrator | Self-modification allowed via release channels. New builds must pass canary tests in isolation before promotion to `:stable`. Fleet hot-reloads from `:stable`, never from `:testing`. |\n115\t| ~20 worker practical limit (EX44) | Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated. Staggered launch is default. |\n116\t| Bead granularity affects success rate | Document guidelines but don't enforce — this is a bead authoring concern, not orchestration. |\n117\t\n118\t---\n119\t\n120\t# State Machine\n121\t\n122\tThe worker loop is a finite state machine. Every state has defined entry conditions, actions, and exit transitions. There are no implicit states or fallthrough paths.\n123\t\n124\t## Worker States\n125\t\n126\t```\n127\t                    ┌──────────┐\n128\t                    │  BOOTING │\n129\t BOOTING\n181\t\n182\t**Entry:** Worker process started.\n183\t\n184\t**Actions:**\n185\t1. Load configuration (global → workspace → CLI overrides)\n186\t2. Validate bead store connectivity (`br doctor` or equivalent)\n187\t3. Register in worker state registry\n188\t4. Emit `worker.started` telemetry event\n189\t5. Start heartbeat emitter\n190\t\n191\t**Transitions:**\n192\t| Condition | Next State |\n193\t|-----------|-----------|\n194\t| Config loaded, bead store healthy | SELECTING |\n195\t| Config invalid | ERRORED |\n196\t| Bead store unreachable | ERRORED (after retry with backoff) |\n197\t\n198\t### SELECTING\n199\t\n200\t**Entry:** Worker is ready for next bead. This is the strand waterfall entry point.\n201\t\n202\t**Actions:**\n203\t1. Emit heartbeat\n204\t2. Evaluate strands in sequence\n205\t3. First strand that yields a candidate bead wins\n206\t\n207\t**Transitions:**\n208\t| Condition | Next State |\n209\t|-----------|-----------|\n210\t| Candidate bead found | CLAIMING |\n211\t| All strands exhausted | EXHAUSTED |\n212\t| Shutdown signal received | STOPPED |\n213\t\n214\t### CLAIMING\n215\t\n216\t**Entry:** A candidate bead has been selected.\n217\t\n218\t**Actions:**\n219\t1. Acquire workspace claim lock (flock, per-workspace)\n220\t2. Verify bead is still claimable (`br show --json`, check status + assignee)\n221\t3. Attempt atomic claim: `br update <id> --claim --actor <worker-id>`\n222\t4. Release workspace claim lock\n223\t5. Emit `bead.claim.attempted` telemetry\n224\t\n225\t**Transitions:**\n226\t| Condition | Exit Code | Next State |\n227\t|-----------|-----------|-----------|\n228\t| Claim succeeded | 0 | BUILDING |\n229\t| Race lost (already claimed) | 4 | RETRYING |\n230\t| Bead no longer claimable (closed, deferred) | 1 | SELECTING |\n231\t| Bead store error | >0 | SELECTING (after backoff) |\n232\t| Max retries exceeded | — | SELECTING (exclude this bead, reset retry counter) |\n233\t\n234\t### RETRYING\n235\t\n236\t**Entry:** A claim attempt failed due to race condition.\n237\t\n238\t**Actions:**\n239\t1. Increment retry counter for this selection cycle\n240\t2. Add failed bead ID to exclusion set\n241\t3. Emit `bead.claim.race_lost` telemetry\n242\t\n243\t**Transitions:**\n244\t| Condition | Next State |\n245\t|-----------|-----------|\n246\t| Retry count < max_retries (default: 5) | CLAIMING (with next candidate from same strand) |\n247\t| Retry count >= max_retries | SELECTING (reset, move to next strand) |\n248\t\n249\t### BUILDING\n250\t\n251\t**Entry:** Bead is claimed by this worker.\n252\t\n253\t**Actions:**\n254\t1. Read full bead context: title, body, dependencies, labels, workspace path\n255\t2. Read workspace context: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .beads/config.yaml\n256\t3. Construct prompt from template (deterministic: same bead → same prompt)\n257\t4. Include bead ID and `br close <id>` instruction in prompt\n258\t5. Emit `prompt.built` telemetry (bead ID, prompt hash, token estimate)\n259\t\n260\t**Transitions:**\n261\t| Condition | Next State |\n262\t|-----------|-----------|\n263\t| Prompt built successfully | DISPATCHING |\n264\t| Bead context unreadable | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n265\t\n266\t### DISPATCHING\n267\t\n268\t**Entry:** Prompt is ready.\n269\t\n270\t**Actions:**\n271\t1. Load agent adapter configuration (YAML)\n272\t2. Resolve invoke template with prompt, workspace path, environment\n273\t3. Start agent process via rendered command\n274\t4. Record process PID, start time\n275\t5. Emit `agent.dispatched` telemetry (agent name, model, workspace)\n276\t\n277\t**Transitions:**\n278\t| Condition | Next State |\n279\t|-----------|-----------|\n280\t| Agent process started | EXECUTING |\n281\t| Agent binary not found | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n282\t| Adapter config invalid | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n283\t\n284\t### EXECUTING\n285\t\n286\t**Entry:** Agent process is running.\n287\t\n288\t**Actions:**\n289\t1. Wait for agent process to exit\n290\t2. Capture stdout, stderr, exit code\n291\t3. Monitor execution timeout\n292\t4. Continue emitting heartbeats while waiting\n293\t5. Emit `agent.executing` heartbeat telemetry periodically\n294\t\n295\t**Transitions:**\n296\t| Condition | Exit Code | Next State |\n297\t|-----------|-----------|-----------|\n298\t| Agent exited normally | any | HANDLING |\n299\t| Execution timeout exceeded | — | Kill process → HANDLING (outcome: timeout) |\n300\t| Shutdown signal received | — | Kill process → HANDLING (outcome: interrupted) |\n301\t\n302\t### HANDLING\n303\t\n304\t**Entry:** Agent has exited (or was killed). This is where outcome routing happens.\n305\t\n306\t**Actions:**\n307\t1. Classify outcome by exit code\n308\t2. Execute the handler for that outcome class\n309\t3. Emit `bead.outcome` telemetry\n310\t\n311\t**Outcome Table:**\n312\t\n313\t| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler | Bead Action |\n314\t|---------|-----------|---------|-------------|\n315\t| **Success** | 0 | Verify bead was closed by agent. If not, log warning (do not auto-close). | None (agent owns closure) |\n316\t| **Failure** | 1 | Evaluate for mitosis (see Mitosis section). If splittable, split and block parent. If not, release bead (`br update --status open --unassign`). Increment failure count via label. | Split or released |\n317\t| **Timeout** | 124 | Release bead. Add `deferred` label. | Released + deferred |\n318\t| **Crash** | >128 (signal) | Release bead. Create alert bead in workspace. | Released + alert |\n319\t| **Race Lost** | 4 | (Handled at CLAIMING, should not reach here) | N/A |\n320\t| **Interrupted** | — | Release bead. Clean shutdown. | Released |\n321\t| **Agent Not Found** | 127 | Release bead. Emit error. Do not retry (config issue). | Released |\n322\t| **Build Failure** | — | Release bead. Emit error. | Released |\n323\t\n324\t**Agent-owned closure:** NEEDLE does not close beads. The agent is instructed (via prompt) to run `br close <id>` upon successful completion. If the bead is still open after a success exit code, NEEDLE logs a warning but does not intervene. This is a deliberate design choice based on operational experience (see `docs/notes/bead-lifecycle-bugs.md`).\n325\t\n326\t**Transitions:**\n327\t| Condition | Next State |\n328\t|-----------|-----------|\n329\t| Outcome processed | LOGGING |\n330\t\n331\t### LOGGING\n332\t\n333\t**Entry:** Outcome has been handled.\n334\t\n335\t**Actions:**\n336\t1. Record effort: elapsed time, exit code, token count (if extractable), estimated cost\n337\t2. Emit `bead.completed` or `bead.released` telemetry\n338\t3. Update worker state registry (beads processed, current streak)\n339\t4. Reset retry counter and exclusion set\n340\t\n341\t**Transitions:**\n342\t| Condition | Next State |\n343\t|-----------|-----------|\n344\t| Logging complete | SELECTING |\n345\t\n346\t### EXHAUSTED\n347\t\n348\t**Entry:** All strands returned no work.\n349\t\n350\t**Actions:**\n351\t1. Emit `worker.exhausted` telemetry\n352\t2. If `idle_timeout` configured, start countdown\n353\t3. If `idle_action` is `wait`, sleep with exponential backoff (max 60s)\n354\t4. If `idle_action` is `exit`, terminate\n355\t\n356\t**Transitions:**\n357\t| Condition | Next State |\n358\t|-----------|-----------|\n359\t| Backoff expired, retry strands | SELECTING |\n360\t| Idle timeout exceeded | STOPPED |\n361\t| Shutdown signal received | STOPPED |\n362\t\n363\t### STOPPED\n364\t\n365\t**Entry:** Graceful shutdown.\n366\t\n367\t**Actions:**\n368\t1. Release any claimed bead\n369\t2. Deregister from worker state registry\n370\t3. Stop heartbeat emitter\n371\t4. Emit `worker.stopped` telemetry\n372\t5. Exit process\n373\t\n374\t**Transitions:** None (terminal).\n375\t\n376\t### ERRORED\n377\t\n378\t**Entry:** Unrecoverable error.\n379\t\n380\t**Actions:**\n381\t1. Release any claimed bead (best-effort)\n382\t2. Emit `worker.errored` telemetry with error details\n383\t3. Deregister from worker state registry (best-effort)\n384\t4. Exit process with non-zero code\n385\t\n386\t**Transitions:** None (terminal).\n387\t\n388\t## Error Model\n389\t\n390\tErrors are classified into three tiers:\n391\t\n392\t### Tier 1: Transient (retry)\n393\t\n394\tTemporary failures that resolve on their own. The worker retries with backoff.\n395\t\n396\t- Bead store temporarily unreachable\n397\t- Claim race lost\n398\t- Lock contention timeout\n399\t- Agent timeout (may succeed on re-dispatch)\n400\t\n401\t### Tier 2: Bead-scoped (release and continue)\n402\t\n403\tFailures specific to one bead. Release it and move on.\n404\t\n405\t- Agent exited with failure\n406\t- Prompt build failed (bead context unreadable)\n407\t- Agent binary missing\n408\t\n409\t### Tier 3: Worker-scoped (exit)\n410\t\n411\tFailures that affect the worker's ability to function. Exit and let the fleet manager handle it.\n412\t\n413\t- Configuration invalid\n414\t- Bead store persistently unreachable\n415\t- Filesystem full\n416\t- Heartbeat file unwritable\n417\t\n418\t## Invariants\n419\t\n420\tThese must hold at all times. Violation of any invariant is a bug.\n421\t\n422\t1. **A worker holds at most one claimed bead.** There is no pipelining or parallel execution within a single worker.\n423\t\n424\t2. **A claimed bead is always released.** Every path through HANDLING releases the bead unless the agent closed it. There is no path where a bead remains claimed after the worker moves to SELECTING.\n425\t\n426\t3. **Heartbeat is continuous.** From BOOTING to STOPPED/ERRORED, the worker emits heartbeats. A gap in heartbeats means the worker is stuck or dead.\n427\t\n428\t4. **Telemetry is emitted for every state transition.** Silent transitions do not exist.\n429\t\n430\t5. **The exclusion set is bounded.** It is cleared on every transition to SELECTING. It cannot grow unboundedly within a selection cycle because max_retries is finite.\n431\t\n432\t6. **Shutdown is always graceful when possible.** SIGTERM triggers STOPPED, not ERRORED. Only SIGKILL causes ungraceful termination, and heartbeat TTL handles that case.\n433\t\n434\t---\n435\t\n436\t# Architecture\n437\t\n438\t## Module Boundaries\n439\t\n440\tNEEDLE is organized into crates (Rust) or packages (Go) with strict dependency rules. No circular dependencies. Each module has a single responsibility.\n441\t\n442\t```\n443\tneedle (binary)\n444\t├── cli/              CLI parsing, session management\n445\t├── worker/           Worker loop, state machine\n446\t├── strand/           Strand waterfall evaluation\n447\t│   └── splice/       Worker failure documentation\n448\t├── claim/            Atomic claiming, lock management\n449\t├── prompt/           Prompt construction from bead context\n450\t├── dispatch/         Agent adapter loading, process execution\n451\t├── outcome/          Exit code classification, outcome handlers\n452\t├── commit_hook/      Bead-Id trailer injection for git commits\n453\t├── telemetry/        Structured event emission, sinks\n454\t├── health/           Heartbeat, stuck detection, peer monitoring\n455\t├── config/           Hierarchical configuration loading\n456\t├── bead_store/       Abstract bead backend interface\n457\t└── types/            Shared types, error definitions\n458\t```\n459\t\n460\t### Dependency Graph\n461\t\n462\t```\n463\tcli ──► worker ──► strand ──► bead_store\n464\t                │           │\n465\t                │           └──► splice ──► bead_store\n466\t                │                               ├──► telemetry\n467\t                │                               └──► health\n468\t                │\n469\t                ├──► claim ─┘\n470\t                │\n471\t                ├──► prompt ──► bead_store\n472\t                │\n473\t                ├──► dispatch\n474\t                │\n475\t                ├──► outcome ──► bead_store\n476\t                │               ├──► telemetry\n477\t                │               └──► health\n478\t                │\n479\t                ├──► commit_hook ──► types\n480\t                │\n481\t                ├──► telemetry\n482\t                │\n483\t                └──► health ──► telemetry\n484\t\n485\tconfig ◄── (all modules)\n486\ttypes  ◄── (all modules)\n487\t```\n488\t\n489\t**Rule:** Arrows point from dependent to dependency. No module depends on `cli` or `worker` except through the binary entry point. `telemetry`, `config`, and `types` are leaf dependencies available to all modules.\n490\t\n491\t## Data Flow\n492\t\n493\t### Primary Loop\n494\t\n495\t```\n496\tbead_store ──[candidates]──► strand ──[bead_id]──► claim ──[claimed_bead]──►\n497\tprompt ──[prompt_string]──► dispatch ──[process]──► worker(wait) ──►\n498\toutcome ──[result]──► bead_store + telemetry\n499\t```\n500\t\n501\t### Telemetry Flow\n502\t\n503\t```\n504\t                    ┌─────────────────────────┐\n505\t                    │    Telemetry Collector   │\n506\t                    └────────────┬────────────┘\n507\t                                 │\n508\t              ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐\n509\t              ▼                  ▼                   ▼\n510\t        ┌──────────┐     ┌────────────┐      ┌──────────┐\n511\t        │ File Sink│     │ Stdout Sink│      │ Hook Sink│\n512\t        │ (JSONL)  │     │ (human)    │      │ (webhook)│\n513\t        └──────────┘     └────────────┘      └──────────┘\n514\t```\n515\t\n516\t### Configuration Flow\n517\t\n518\t```\n519\t  CLI args ──► env vars ──► workspace .needle.yaml ──► global ~/.needle/config.yaml ──► defaults\n520\t  (highest)                                                                              (lowest)\n521\t```\n522\t\n523\t## Module Specifications\n524\t\n525\t### bead_store\n526\t\n527\tAbstract interface to any bead backend. The primary implementation wraps the `br` CLI, but the trait allows future backends (direct SQLite, HTTP API, etc.).\n528\t\n529\t```\n530\ttrait BeadStore {\n531\t    fn ready(workspace: &Path, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>\n532\t    fn show(id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead>\n533\t    fn claim(id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>\n534\t    fn release(id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>\n535\t    fn labels(id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>>\n536\t    fn add_label(id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()>\n537\t    fn doctor_repair() -> Result<RepairReport>\n538\t}\n539\t\n540\tenum ClaimResult {\n541\t    Claimed(Bead),\n542\t    RaceLost { claimed_by: String },\n543\t    NotClaimable { reason: String },\n544\t}\n545\t```\n546\t\n547\t**Design notes:**\n548\t- All methods return `Result`. Silent failures do not exist.\n549\t- `ClaimResult` is an enum, not a boolean. The caller must handle each variant.\n550\t- `ready()` accepts filters (status, assignee, labels, workspace) to push filtering to the backend.\n551\t- The `br` CLI implementation shells out to `br` with `--json` and parses output via `serde_json`.\n552\t- JSON parsing failures are explicit errors, not empty results (learned from starvation false positives).\n553\t\n554\t### claim\n555\t\n556\tWraps `bead_store.claim()` with workspace-level serialization and retry logic.\n557\t\n558\t```\n559\tstruct Claimer {\n560\t    bead_store: Box<dyn BeadStore>,\n561\t    lock_dir: PathBuf,       // per-workspace flock directory\n562\t    max_retries: u32,        // default: 5\n563\t    retry_backoff_ms: u64,   // default: 100\n564\t}\n565\t\n566\timpl Claimer {\n567\t    fn claim_next(\n568\t        &self,\n569\t        candidates: &[Bead],\n570\t        actor: &str,\n571\t        exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,\n572\t    ) -> Result<ClaimOutcome>\n573\t}\n574\t\n575\tenum ClaimOutcome {\n576\t    Claimed(Bead),\n577\t    AllRaceLost,\n578\t    NoCandidates,\n579\t    StoreError(Error),\n580\t}\n581\t```\n582\t\n583\t**Design notes:**\n584\t- The flock is per-workspace, not per-bead. This serializes all claim operations within a workspace, preventing thundering herd (learned from `docs/notes/claim-race-conditions.md`).\n585\t- The lock is held only for the duration of the `br update --claim` call, not for the entire bead execution.\n586\t- Retry logic is internal to the Claimer. The caller receives a final `ClaimOutcome`.\n587\t\n588\t### strand\n589\t\n590\tEvaluates the strand waterfall and returns the next action.\n591\t\n592\t```\n593\ttrait Strand {\n594\t    fn name(&self) -> &str\n595\t    fn enabled(&self, config: &Config) -> bool\n596\t    fn evaluate(&self, context: &WorkerContext) -> Result<StrandResult>\n597\t}\n598\t\n599\tenum StrandResult {\n600\t    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),    // candidates for claiming\n601\t    WorkCreated,              // strand created new beads (e.g., weave)\n602\t    NoWork,                   // fall through to next strand\n603\t    Error(StrandError),       // strand failed, fall through\n604\t}\n605\t```\n606\t\n607\tEach strand implements the trait. The runner evaluates them in order:\n608\t\n609\t```\n610\tfn run_strands(strands: &[Box<dyn Strand>], ctx: &WorkerContext) -> StrandWaterfallResult {\n611\t    for strand in strands {\n612\t        if !strand.enabled(&ctx.config) { continue; }\n613\t        match strand.evaluate(ctx)? {\n614\t            StrandResult::BeadFound(candidates) => return Ok(candidates),\n615\t            StrandResult::WorkCreated => return Ok(/* re-evaluate from strand 1 */),\n616\t            StrandResult::NoWork => continue,\n617\t            StrandResult::Error(e) => { emit_telemetry(e); continue; }\n618\t        }\n619\t    }\n620\t    StrandWaterfallResult::Exhausted\n621\t}\n622\t```\n623\t\n624\t### dispatch\n625\t\n626\tLoads agent adapters and executes the agent process.\n627\t\n628\t```\n629\tstruct Dispatcher {\n630\t    adapters: HashMap<String, AgentAdapter>,\n631\t}\n632\t\n633\tstruct AgentAdapter {\n634\t    name: String,\n635\t    invoke_template: String,   // e.g., \"cd {workspace} && claude --print\"\n636\t    input_method: InputMethod,  // Stdin, File, Args\n637\t    timeout: Duration,\n638\t    environment: HashMap<String, String>,\n639\t}\n640\t\n641\tenum InputMethod {\n642\t    Stdin,                      // pipe prompt to stdin\n643\t    File { path_template: String },  // write prompt to file, pass path\n644\t    Args { flag: String },      // pass prompt as --flag value\n645\t}\n646\t\n647\tstruct ExecutionResult {\n648\t    exit_code: i32,\n649\t    stdout: String,\n650\t    stderr: String,\n651\t    elapsed: Duration,\n652\t    pid: u32,\n653\t}\n654\t```\n655\t\n656\t**Design notes:**\n657\t- Adapters are loaded from YAML config files. Adding a new agent requires only a new YAML file.\n658\t- The invoke template is rendered with variables: `{workspace}`, `{prompt_file}`, `{bead_id}`, `{model}`.\n659\t- The dispatcher does not interpret agent output. It captures raw exit code, stdout, and stderr, then passes them to the outcome handler.\n660\t- Timeout is enforced by the dispatcher, not the agent. If the agent exceeds the timeout, the dispatcher kills the process and returns exit code 124.\n661\t\n662\t### outcome\n663\t\n664\tClassifies the agent's exit and routes to the appropriate handler.\n665\t\n666\t```\n667\tenum Outcome {\n668\t    Success,           // exit 0\n669\t    Failure,           // exit 1\n670\t    Timeout,           // exit 124 (set by dispatcher)\n671\t    Crash(i32),        // exit >128 (signal)\n672\t    AgentNotFound,     // exit 127\n673\t    Interrupted,       // shutdown signal during execution\n674\t}\n675\t\n676\tfn classify(result: &ExecutionResult, was_interrupted: bool) -> Outcome {\n677\t    if was_interrupted { return Outcome::Interrupted; }\n678\t    match result.exit_code {\n679\t        0   => Outcome::Success,\n680\t        1   => Outcome::Failure,\n681\t        124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n682\t        127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n683\t        c if c > 128 => Outcome::Crash(c),\n684\t        _   => Outcome::Failure,  // treat unknown codes as failure\n685\t    }\n686\t}\n687\t```\n688\t\n689\t**Design notes:**\n690\t- The match is exhaustive. Every exit code maps to exactly one outcome.\n691\t- The `Outcome` enum is the sole input to the handler. There is no ad-hoc exit code checking elsewhere.\n692\t- `Outcome::Success` does NOT mean the bead is closed. It means the agent exited cleanly. Bead closure is the agent's responsibility.\n693\t\n694\t### telemetry\n695\t\n696\t```\n697\tfn emit(event: TelemetryEvent)\n698\t\n699\tstruct TelemetryEvent {\n700\t    timestamp: DateTime<Utc>,\n701\t    worker_id: String,\n702\t    event_type: String,       // e.g., \"bead.claim.attempted\"\n703\t    bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n704\t    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n705\t    data: serde_json::Value,  // event-specific payload\n706\t    duration_ms: Option<u64>,\n707\t    trace_id: Option<TraceId>,   // W3C trace ID of enclosing span, if OTLP sink enabled\n708\t    span_id: Option<SpanId>,     // W3C span ID of enclosing span, if OTLP sink enabled\n709\t}\n710\t\n711\ttrait Sink: Send + Sync {\n712\t    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()>;\n713\t    fn flush(&self, deadline: Duration) -> Result<()>;\n714\t}\n715\t\n716\t// Built-in sinks: FileSink, StdoutSink, HookSink, OtlpSink.\n717\t// OtlpSink wraps the OpenTelemetry SDK (traces + metrics + logs providers)\n718\t// and translates TelemetryEvent into the appropriate signal per the\n719\t// Semantic Mapping table in the Telemetry chapter.\n720\t```\n721\t\n722\t### health\n723\t\n724\t```\n725\tstruct HealthMonitor {\n726\t    heartbeat_interval: Duration,    // default: 30s\n727\t    heartbeat_ttl: Duration,         // default: 5min\n728\t    heartbeat_dir: PathBuf,          // ~/.needle/state/heartbeats/\n729\t    peer_check_interval: Duration,   // default: 60s\n730\t}\n731\t\n732\timpl HealthMonitor {\n733\t    fn emit_heartbeat(&self, state: &WorkerState) -> Result<()>\n734\t    fn check_peers(&self) -> Result<Vec<PeerStatus>>\n735\t    fn cleanup_stale_claims(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore) -> Result<u32>\n736\t}\n737\t\n738\tenum PeerStatus {\n739\t    Alive { last_seen: DateTime<Utc>, current_bead: Option<BeadId> },\n740\t    Stale { last_seen: DateTime<Utc>, claimed_bead: Option<BeadId> },\n741\t    Dead { heartbeat_file: PathBuf },\n742\t}\n743\t```\n744\t\n745\t### commit_hook\n746\t\n747\tInjects `Bead-Id:` trailers into git commits after successful bead closure, for HOOP bead_commit_index integration.\n748\t\n749\t```\n750\tasync fn inject_bead_id_trailer(\n751\t    workspace: &Path,\n752\t    bead_id: &BeadId,\n753\t    pre_dispatch_head: &str,\n754\t) -> Result<()>\n755\t\n756\tfn git_head(workspace: &str) -> Result<String>\n757\t```\n758\t\n759\t**Functionality:**\n760\t- When a bead closes with a commit artifact (agent made commits), NEEDLE amends the latest commit to include a `Bead-Id: <id>` trailer\n761\t- Only acts when HEAD moved since `pre_dispatch_head` (i.e. the agent made at least one commit)\n762\t- Idempotent: checks if trailer is already present before injecting\n763\t- Returns `Ok(())` in all no-op cases (not a git repo, no new commits, trailer already present)\n764\t\n765\t**Trailer format:**\n766\t```\n767\tBead-Id: nd-a3f8\n768\t```\n769\t\n770\t**Integration context:**\n771\t- HOOP's `bead_commit_index` picks up the trailer via `git log --format=%(trailers:key=Bead-Id,valueonly,separator=,)`\n772\t- Enables bidirectional traceability: beads → commits and commits → beads\n773\t- Executed after successful bead close, before returning to SELECTING state\n774\t\n775\t**Timeouts:**\n776\t- `git rev-parse HEAD`: 10s timeout\n777\t- `git commit --amend`: 30s timeout\n778\t\n779\t**Design notes:**\n780\t- Errors are logged as non-fatal warnings; they do not fail the bead processing cycle\n781\t- The trailer is appended via `git commit --amend --no-edit --trailer \"Bead-Id: <id>\"`\n782\t- Multiple beads can be tracked in a single commit (comma-separated in trailer value)\n783\t\n784\t## Binary Structure\n785\t\n786\tNEEDLE is a single binary with subcommands:\n787\t\n788\t```\n789\tneedle run [--workspace PATH] [--agent NAME] [--count N] [--identifier NAME]\n790\tneedle stop [--all | --identifier NAME]\n791\tneedle list [--format table|json]\n792\tneedle attach <identifier>\n793\tneedle status [--format table|json]\n794\tneedle config [--get KEY | --set KEY VALUE]\n795\tneedle doctor [--repair]\n796\tneedle version\n797\t```\n798\t\n799\t### Session Management\n800\t\n801\t`needle run` creates tmux sessions for each worker. Session naming follows the pattern:\n802\t\n803\t```\n804\tneedle-{agent}-{provider}-{model}-{identifier}\n805\t```\n806\t\n807\tExamples:\n808\t```\n809\tneedle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha\n810\tneedle-opencode-alibaba-qwen-bravo\n811\tneedle-codex-openai-gpt4-charlie\n812\t```\n813\t\n814\t`--count=N` launches N workers with sequential NATO alphabet identifiers (alpha, bravo, charlie, ...). Workers are launched with staggered delay (default: 2s between launches) to prevent thundering herd on startup (learned from `docs/notes/operational-fleet-lessons.md`).\n815\t\n816\t### CLI Help System\n817\t\n818\tEvery subcommand and flag is discoverable via `--help` or `-h`. Help text is embedded in the binary and generated from the same source as the CLI parser (e.g., `clap` derive macros in Rust).\n819\t\n820\t**Top-level help:**\n821\t\n822\t```\n823\t$ needle --help\n824\t\n825\tNEEDLE — Navigates Every Enqueued Deliverable, Logs Effort\n826\t\n827\tDeterministic bead processing with explicit outcome paths.\n828\t\n829\tUsage: needle <COMMAND>\n830\t\n831\tCommands:\n832\t  run          Launch worker(s) to process beads\n833\t  stop         Stop running worker(s)\n834\t  list         List active workers\n835\t  attach       Attach to a worker's tmux session\n836\t  status       Show fleet status, bead counts, and cost summary\n837\t  config       View or modify configuration\n838\t  doctor       Check system health and repair\n839\t  test-agent   Validate an agent adapter\n840\t  logs         Query telemetry logs\n841\t  rollback     Roll back to previous stable binary\n842\t  version      Show version information\n843\t  help         Print this message or the help of a subcommand\n844\t\n845\tOptions:\n846\t  -h, --help     Print help\n847\t  -V, --version  Print version\n848\t```\n849\t\n850\t**Subcommand help (example):**\n851\t\n852\t```\n853\t$ needle run --help\n854\t\n855\tLaunch worker(s) to process beads\n856\t\n857\tUsage: needle run [OPTIONS]\n858\t\n859\tOptions:\n860\t  -w, --workspace <PATH>     Workspace to process beads from [default: config value]\n861\t  -a, --agent <NAME>         Agent adapter to use [default: config value]\n862\t  -c, --count <N>            Number of workers to launch [default: 1]\n863\t  -i, --identifier <NAME>    Worker identifier (overrides NATO naming)\n864\t  -t, --timeout <SECONDS>    Agent execution timeout [default: config value]\n865\t      --resume               Resume an existing worker session (used by hot-reload)\n866\t  -h, --help                 Print help\n867\t```\n868\t\n869\t**Design notes:**\n870\t- Every flag has a one-line description\n871\t- Default values shown in brackets (sourced from config)\n872\t- Subcommand grouping follows the lifecycle: launch → monitor → operate → maintain\n873\t- `needle help <command>` and `needle <command> --help` are equivalent\n874\t- Help output is plain text, no colors, suitable for piping to other tools or agents\n875\t\n876\t---\n877\t\n878\t# Strand Waterfall\n879\t\n880\tStrands are NEEDLE's strategy for finding work. They are evaluated in strict sequence — the first strand that yields actionable work wins. When a strand returns `NoWork`, the worker falls through to the next.\n881\t\n882\tThe waterfall is the answer to \"what does a worker do when it has no beads?\" It is not a priority system for beads (that's handled by deterministic ordering within each strand). It is a priority system for *strategies*.\n883\t\n884\t## Waterfall Sequence\n885\t\n886\t```\n887\t  Strand 1: PLUCK ──── primary work from assigned workspace\n888\t       │ no work\n889\t       ▼\n890\t  Strand 2: MEND ───── cleanup: stale claims, orphaned locks, health\n891\t       │ nothing to clean\n892\t       ▼\n893\t  Strand 3: EXPLORE ── look for work in other configured workspaces\n894\t       │ no work\n895\t       ▼\n896\t  Strand 4: WEAVE ──── create beads from documentation gaps (opt-in)\n897\t       │ no gaps or disabled\n898\t       ▼\n899\t  Strand 5: UNRAVEL ── propose alternatives for HUMAN-blocked beads (opt-in)\n900\t       │ none or disabled\n901\t       ▼\n902\t  Strand 6: PULSE ──── codebase health scan, auto-generate beads (opt-in)\n903\t       │ no issues or disabled\n904\t       ▼\n905\t  Strand 7: REFLECT ── consolidate learnings from recent beads\n906\t       │ consolidation complete or not needed\n907\t       ▼\n908\t  Strand 8: SPLICE ──── worker failure documentation\n909\t       │ no failures\n910\t       ▼\n911\t  Strand 9: KNOT ───── alert human, enter backoff\n912\t       │\n913\t       ▼\n914\t  → EXHAUSTED (backoff and retry from Strand 1)\n915\t```\n916\t\n917\t## Strand 1: Pluck\n918\t\n919\t**Purpose:** Process beads from the worker's assigned workspace. This is the primary work strand and will handle >90% of all bead processing.\n920\t\n921\t**Invokes agent:** Yes.\n922\t\n923\t**Entry condition:** Worker has an assigned workspace with a `.beads/` directory.\n924\t\n925\t**Algorithm:**\n926\t1. Query bead store: `br ready --unassigned --json` in workspace\n927\t2. Filter: exclude beads with labels `deferred`, `human`, `blocked`\n928\t3. Filter: exclude beads in the current retry exclusion set\n929\t4. Sort: priority (ascending, 0 = highest), then creation time (ascending, oldest first)\n930\t5. Return sorted candidates for claiming\n931\t\n932\t**Exit conditions:**\n933\t| Result | Action |\n934\t|--------|--------|\n935\t| Candidates found | Return `BeadFound(candidates)` → worker proceeds to CLAIMING |\n936\t| No candidates (queue empty) | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 2 |\n937\t| Bead store error | Emit telemetry, return `Error` → fall through to Strand 2 |\n938\t\n939\t**Determinism guarantee:** The sort key `(priority, created_at)` produces the same ordering for all workers viewing the same queue state. Workers will compete for the same top-priority bead, and the claim mechanism resolves contention.\n940\t\n941\t## Strand 2: Mend\n942\t\n943\t**Purpose:** Maintenance and cleanup operations that keep the bead store healthy. Runs before Explore because cleaning up stale claims or broken dependencies in the home workspace may unblock beads here — no need to roam if local work is just stuck.\n944\t\n945\t**Invokes agent:** No.\n946\t\n947\t**Entry condition:** Strand 1 returned no work.\n948\t\n949\t**Algorithm:**\n950\t1. **Stale claim cleanup:** Find beads with status `in_progress` where the assigned worker has no active heartbeat (TTL expired). Release them.\n951\t2. **Orphaned lock cleanup:** Find workspace lock files older than TTL. Remove them.\n952\t3. **Dependency cleanup:** Find closed beads that are still listed as blockers on open beads. Remove the stale dependency links.\n953\t4. **Database health:** Run `br doctor` (not `--repair` unless errors found).\n954\t\n955\t**Exit conditions:**\n956\t| Result | Action |\n957\t|--------|--------|\n958\t| Cleanup performed | Return `WorkCreated` → restart from Strand 1 (released beads may now be claimable) |\n959\t| Nothing to clean | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 3 |\n960\t\n961\t**Design notes (from `docs/notes/bead-lifecycle-bugs.md`):**\n962\t- Stale dependency links caused permanent blocking in NEEDLE-deprecated. Mend must clean these.\n963\t- Distinguish \"did work\" from \"found nothing\" — v1 had an infinite loop where mend returned success on failed releases.\n964\t\n965\t## Strand 3: Explore\n966\t\n967\t**Purpose:** Discover work in other configured workspaces when the home workspace is empty and clean.\n968\t\n969\t**Invokes agent:** No. Explore only finds candidates — execution happens back through the standard CLAIMING → DISPATCHING flow.\n970\t\n971\t**Entry condition:** Strands 1-2 returned no work. Explore is enabled in config. At least one additional workspace is configured.\n972\t\n973\t**Algorithm:**\n974\t1. Read configured workspace list from config (explicit paths, no filesystem scanning)\n975\t2. For each workspace (in configured order):\n976\t   a. Check `.beads/` directory exists\n977\t   b. Query `br ready --unassigned --json`\n978\t   c. If candidates found, return them with workspace context\n979\t3. If no workspace has work, return `NoWork`\n980\t\n981\t**Exit conditions:**\n982\t| Result | Action |\n983\t|--------|--------|\n984\t| Candidates found in another workspace | Return `BeadFound(candidates)` with workspace override |\n985\t| No candidates in any workspace | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 4 |\n986\t\n987\t**Design notes (from `docs/notes/explore-strand-bugs.md`):**\n988\t- **No filesystem scanning.** NEEDLE-deprecated's `find`-based discovery caused 35+ CPU load with 40 workers. Workspaces must be explicitly configured.\n989\t- **No upward traversal.** The v1 explore strand walked up parent directories to `/home`, then `/`. This is eliminated.\n990\t- **Workspace list is static** for the duration of a session. It is read from config at boot and not re-evaluated.\n991\t- **Workers do not permanently relocate.** If a worker finds work in another workspace, it processes that bead and returns to its home workspace for the next cycle.\n992\t\n993\t## Strand 4: Weave (opt-in)\n994\t\n995\t**Purpose:** Analyze workspace documentation for gaps and create new beads to address them.\n996\t\n997\t**Invokes agent:** Yes — uses the agent to analyze documentation and propose beads.\n998\t\n999\t**Entry condition:** Strands 1-3 (Pluck, Mend, Explore) returned no work. Weave is explicitly enabled in workspace config (`strands.weave.enabled: true`).\n1000\t\n1001\t**Algorithm:**\n1002\t1. Identify documentation files (README, AGENTS.md, docs/, etc.)\n1003\t2. Dispatch agent with gap-analysis prompt\n1004\t3. Agent proposes new beads (as structured output)\n1005\t4. Create beads via bead store\n1006\t5. Return `WorkCreated` → restart from Strand 1\n1007\t\n1008\t**Guardrails (from `docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md`):**\n1009\t- **Max beads per weave run:** Configurable, default 5. Prevents unbounded bead creation.\n1010\t- **Cooldown period:** Minimum time between weave runs per workspace, default 24h.\n1011\t- **Seen-issues deduplication:** Track previously created weave beads to prevent duplicates.\n1012\t- **Workspace exclusion:** Weave is disabled for NEEDLE's own workspace by default. Workers must not create work for their own orchestrator without human approval.\n1013\t- **Human review label:** Weave-created beads are labeled `weave-generated` for easy filtering.\n1014\t\n1015\t**Exit conditions:**\n1016\t| Result | Action |\n1017\t|--------|--------|\n1018\t| Beads created | Return `WorkCreated` → restart from Strand 1 |\n1019\t| No gaps found | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 5 |\n1020\t| Disabled | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 5 |\n1021\t\n1022\t## Strand 5: Unravel (opt-in)\n1023\t\n1024\t**Purpose:** For beads labeled `human` (requiring human decision), propose alternative approaches that an agent could execute instead.\n1025\t\n1026\t**Invokes agent:** Yes — uses the agent to analyze the blocked bead and propose workarounds.\n1027\t\n1028\t**Entry condition:** Strands 1-4 returned no work. Unravel is explicitly enabled. There are beads with `human` label in the workspace.\n1029\t\n1030\t**Algorithm:**\n1031\t1. Query beads with `human` label\n1032\t2. For each (up to `max_unravel_per_run`, default 3):\n1033\t   a. Dispatch agent with the bead context and a prompt asking for alternative approaches\n1034\t   b. If agent proposes viable alternatives, create child beads with `alternative` label\n1035\t   c. Do NOT close or modify the original `human` bead\n1036\t3. Return `WorkCreated` if alternatives were created\n1037\t\n1038\t**Guardrails:**\n1039\t- Original `human` bead is never modified or closed\n1040\t- Alternative beads are linked as children (informational, not blocking)\n1041\t- Max alternatives per `human` bead: configurable, default 2\n1042\t- Cooldown: don't re-analyze a `human` bead that was analyzed within the last 7 days\n1043\t\n1044\t**Exit conditions:**\n1045\t| Result | Action |\n1046\t|--------|--------|\n1047\t| Alternatives created | Return `WorkCreated` → restart from Strand 1 |\n1048\t| No `human` beads or no alternatives viable | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 6 |\n1049\t| Disabled | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 6 |\n1050\t\n1051\t## Strand 6: Pulse (opt-in)\n1052\t\n1053\t**Purpose:** Scan the codebase for health issues (stale TODOs, missing tests, dependency drift, linting) and create beads for significant findings.\n1054\t\n1055\t**Invokes agent:** Yes — uses the agent (or external tools) to scan the codebase.\n1056\t\n1057\t**Entry condition:** Strands 1-5 returned no work. Pulse is explicitly enabled. Cooldown has expired.\n1058\t\n1059\t**Algorithm:**\n1060\t1. Run configured scanners (linters, test coverage, dependency checkers, TODO scanners)\n1061\t2. Compare results against previous scan (stored in `~/.needle/state/pulse/`)\n1062\t3. For new issues exceeding severity threshold, create beads\n1063\t4. Update last-scan state\n1064\t\n1065\t**Guardrails:**\n1066\t- **Max beads per pulse run:** Configurable, default 10\n1067\t- **Cooldown:** Default 48h between scans\n1068\t- **Severity threshold:** Only create beads for issues above configured severity\n1069\t- **Deduplication:** Track seen issues to prevent duplicate beads across scans\n1070\t- **Workspace exclusion:** Same as Weave — disabled for NEEDLE's own workspace by default\n1071\t\n1072\t**Exit conditions:**\n1073\t| Result | Action |\n1074\t|--------|--------|\n1075\t| Beads created | Return `WorkCreated` → restart from Strand 1 |\n1076\t| No new issues | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 7 |\n1077\t| Disabled | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 7 |\n1078\t\n1079\t## Strand 7: Reflect (opt-in)\n1080\t\n1081\t**Purpose:** Consolidate learnings from recent bead work into a shared knowledge base (`.beads/learnings.md`), promoting recurring patterns to reusable skill files. This meta-analysis strand ensures that insights from completed work are captured and made available to future work.\n1082\t\n1083\t**Invokes agent:** Yes — uses a consolidation-specific prompt.\n1084\t\n1085\t**Entry condition:** Strands 1-6 returned no work. Reflect is explicitly enabled in workspace config (`strands.reflect.enabled: true`). At least N beads have been closed since last consolidation (configurable, default: 10). At least T hours since last consolidation (configurable, default: 24).\n1086\t\n1087\t**Algorithm (KAIROS-inspired four-phase cycle):**\n1088\t\n1089\t1. **Orient:** Read current `.beads/learnings.md` and existing skill files in `.beads/skills/`. Check file sizes to ensure they're within bounds.\n1090\t2. **Gather:** Read bead close bodies from `.beads/issues.jsonl` for beads closed since last consolidation. Read available traces for failed beads to capture failure patterns.\n1091\t3. **Consolidate:**\n1092\t   - Extract retrospective blocks from close bodies\n1093\t   - Identify patterns across multiple beads (same failure mode, same codebase quirk, workaround that works)\n1094\t   - Merge new learnings into `.beads/learnings.md`, deduplicating against existing entries\n1095\t   - Convert relative references to absolute (bead IDs, dates)\n1096\t   - If a learning appears 3+ times across different beads, promote to a skill file in `.beads/skills/`\n1097\t   - If a learning contradicts an existing entry, resolve in favor of the newer evidence\n1098\t4. **Prune:**\n1099\t   - Remove entries older than 90 days without reinforcement\n1100\t   - Compress similar entries into single entries\n1101\t   - Ensure total learnings stay under 80 entries (configurable)\n1102\t\n1103\t**Guardrails:**\n1104\t- **Cooldown:** Minimum 24 hours between consolidation runs (configurable)\n1105\t- **Max learnings created per run:** 10 (configurable)\n1106\t- **Max skills promoted per run:** 3 (configurable)\n1107\t- **Read-only on CLAUDE.md:** The consolidation agent receives the workspace CLAUDE.md as context but MUST NOT modify it. CLAUDE.md changes require explicit human approval.\n1108\t- **Workspace exclusion:** Reflect is disabled for NEEDLE's own workspace by default. Workers must not modify their own orchestrator's knowledge base without human approval.\n1109\t\n1110\t**Exit conditions:**\n1111\t| Result | Action |\n1112\t|--------|--------|\n1113\t| Consolidation performed | Return `WorkCreated` → restart from Strand 1 (learnings may unblock new work) |\n1114\t| Not enough data since last run | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 8 |\n1115\t| Disabled or cooldown active | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 8 |\n1116\t\n1117\t**Telemetry:**\n1118\t| Event Type | Emitted When | Data Fields |\n1119\t|------------|-------------|-------------|\n1120\t| `reflect.started` | Consolidation starts | `beads_since_last`, `current_learnings_count` |\n1121\t| `reflect.consolidated` | Consolidation completes | `learnings_added`, `learnings_pruned`, `skills_promoted`, `contradictions_resolved` |\n1122\t| `reflect.skipped` | Consolidation skipped | `reason` (cooldown, insufficient data, disabled) |\n1123\t\n1124\t**Learning persistence:** `.beads/learnings.md` is the authoritative source. Workers automatically append it to `context_files` during prompt building (via the Config module's `context_files` discovery). No manual config required — workers always see the latest learnings.\n1125\t\n1126\t**Session transcript analysis:** Reflect analyzes both bead close bodies (structured outcomes) and Claude Code session transcripts (decision-making process) when available. Transcripts are stored as JSONL in `.claude/projects/<project-hash>/<session-uuid>.jsonl` and contain richer signal: failed attempts, tool call sequences, recovery strategies, and decision points.\n1127\t\n1128\t**Integration with prompt building:** If `.beads/learnings.md` exists in a workspace, NEEDLE automatically appends it to `context_files` during prompt building. Workers always see the latest learnings without manual configuration.\n1129\t\n1130\t## Strand 8: Splice\n1131\t\n1132\t**Purpose:** Document worker failures (crashed workers and live-but-looping workers) by creating failure beads in a configured report workspace.\n1133\t\n1134\t**Invokes agent:** No.\n1135\t\n1136\t**Entry condition:** Strand 7 returned no work. Splice is enabled in config (default: true). Heartbeat files exist in the heartbeat directory.\n1137\t\n1138\t**Algorithm:**\n1139\t\n1140\t1. **Scan for dead workers (stale heartbeat + dead tmux session):**\n1141\t   - Read all heartbeat files from the heartbeat directory\n1142\t   - For each heartbeat older than `stale_threshold_secs` (default: 300s):\n1143\t     - Check if the tmux session is still alive\n1144\t     - If session is dead, this is a failed worker\n1145\t\n1146\t2. **Scan for live-but-looping workers (optional, when `detect_live_loops: true`):**\n1147\t   - For each worker with a fresh heartbeat:\n1148\t     - Read the tail of their JSONL log file\n1149\t     - Detect three loop patterns:\n1150\t       - **Claim churn:** Repeated `bead.claim.race_lost` events for the same bead\n1151\t       - **State ping-pong:** Rapid cycling between a small set of states without forward progress\n1152\t       - **Log runaway:** Excessive JSONL growth without `agent.completed` events\n1153\t\n1154\t3. **Create failure beads:**\n1155\t   - For each undocumented failure or loop pattern:\n1156\t     - Create a bead in the configured `report_workspace`\n1157\t     - Include worker details, session info, and evidence in the bead body\n1158\t   - Track documented sessions/loops in `splice_state.json` to prevent duplicates\n1159\t\n1160\t4. **Return `WorkCreated` if any beads were created, otherwise `NoWork`**\n1161\t\n1162\t**Exit conditions:**\n1163\t| Result | Action |\n1164\t|--------|--------|\n1165\t| Failure beads created | Return `WorkCreated` → restart from Strand 1 |\n1166\t| No new failures detected | Return `NoWork` → fall through to Strand 9 |\n1167\t\n1168\t**State persistence:** `splice_state.json` tracks which session IDs and loop patterns have already been documented, preventing duplicate failure beads for the same dead/looping worker.\n1169\t\n1170\t**Loop detection thresholds:**\n1171\t- `claim_churn_threshold`: Number of race-lost events for same bead before flagging (default: 20)\n1172\t- `log_runaway_bytes`: Max JSONL growth in `live_loop_window_secs` without completion (default: 10 MiB)\n1173\t- `live_loop_window_secs`: Time window for log runaway check (default: 300s)\n1174\t\n1175\t## Strand 9: Knot\n1176\t\n1177\t**Purpose:** All work-finding strategies are exhausted. Alert the human and enter backoff.\n1178\t\n1179\t**Invokes agent:** No.\n1180\t\n1181\t**Entry condition:** Strands 1-8 all returned `NoWork`.\n1182\t\n1183\t**Algorithm:**\n1184\t1. Determine alert state:\n1185\t   - **First time exhausted:** Emit `worker.idle` telemetry. Start backoff timer.\n1186\t   - **Repeated exhaustion (>N cycles):** Create alert bead (if not already created within cooldown).\n1187\t2. Verify before alerting (three-state check):\n1188\t   a. **No beads exist:** Queue is genuinely empty. Normal idle.\n1189\t   b. **All beads claimed:** Other workers are busy. Normal contention. Wait.\n1190\t   c. **Beads invisible:** Configuration error (wrong workspace, broken filter). Alert.\n1191\t3. Return `NoWork` → worker enters EXHAUSTED state with backoff\n1192\t\n1193\t**Guardrails (from `docs/notes/worker-starvation-lessons.md`):**\n1194\t- **Verify independently before alerting.** The v1 system had 100% false positive rate because it used the same broken code path for verification.\n1195\t- **Three-state model.** \"No work\" is three different conditions with different responses.
